domain: Holdout engineering: sealed, situated, randomised tests that an agent-built product meets only at test time
ratification_status: DRAFT: not yet ratified by the owner

worldviews.name: Builder: the implementer agent that writes the product and wants its checks to pass
worldviews.applies_when: Use it to predict how a builder could tune the product to a visible check or learn a sealed one early.

worldviews.name: Owner: the person whose words are the promise
worldviews.applies_when: Use it to decide what a holdout must protect and to refuse any promise the owner did not make.

worldviews.name: Participant: the human, agent, seam or future participant who meets the product
worldviews.applies_when: Use it to set a holdout inside the situation of someone who will actually meet the product.

worldviews.name: Auditor: an independent reviewer who reruns and verifies after the test
worldviews.applies_when: Use it to judge whether a verdict, a seal or a parameter proof can be checked by someone who trusts nothing you say.

worldviews.name: Attacker: anyone trying to learn the sealed how or the test-time parameters early
worldviews.applies_when: Use it to find the cheapest way to defeat a seal, a reveal or an evaluator.

categories.name: Owner promises
categories.seam: Owns what the owner promised, in the owner's words; category 02 owns who meets the product.

items.item_name: Promise captured verbatim from the owner
items.detailed_description: Covers the promise a holdout protects. The promise is the owner's own words, quoted with their source and date, never an agent's paraphrase. It matters because a holdout that protects a paraphrase can pass while the owner's intent fails. The signature failure is a summarised promise that quietly drops a condition. Seam: item 0102 governs changes to a promise; category 02 governs the participants a promise is set inside.
synthesis_instructions: Quote each promise verbatim with its source and date before any holdout is planned against it.
Refuse to plan a holdout against a promise that has no verbatim owner source; record it as an open question for the owner.
Never replace the owner's words with a summary in a sealed plan; a summary may sit beside the quote, never instead of it.

internal_evaluation_criteria.question: Does every promise the plan protects carry a verbatim owner quote with source and date?
internal_evaluation_criteria.pass_condition: Each promise in the plan resolves to a quoted owner statement; a promise with only a paraphrase fails.
internal_evaluation_criteria.checklist: [ ] trace one promise from the plan to the owner's quoted words

applicability_signals: The task names what the product must do for its owner
A planning document states goals, guarantees or acceptance conditions
anti_signals: The task asks for implementation work on the product itself

signature_failures.failure: A paraphrased promise drops a condition, so the holdout passes a product that breaks the owner's actual words.
signature_failures.guard: Keep the verbatim quote in the sealed plan and check each holdout against the quote, not the paraphrase.

items.item_name: No invented, widened or softened promise
items.detailed_description: Covers changes to a promise. An agent never invents a promise, widens one to cover more than the owner said, or softens one so it is easier to pass. Only the owner changes a promise, and the change is recorded as a dated owner decision. It matters because a lens or a generator that adds its own promise turns a holdout into the agent's opinion. Seam: item 0101 governs capturing the promise; this item governs every later change.
synthesis_instructions: Refuse any holdout whose expected outcome rests on a promise the owner did not make; name the missing owner source.
Flag any difference between a holdout's expectation and the quoted promise as widening or softening, and send it to the owner.
Record every promise change only as a dated owner decision that quotes the owner.

internal_evaluation_criteria.question: Does any check reach a promise that no owner statement supports?
internal_evaluation_criteria.pass_condition: Every check traces to an owner-approved promise; a check reaching an agent-invented promise fails.
internal_evaluation_criteria.checklist: [ ] list each check's promise and confirm an owner quote or owner decision for it

applicability_signals: A generated holdout or lens proposes a new expectation
Someone suggests relaxing a holdout so the product passes
anti_signals: The owner has recorded the change as a dated decision

signature_failures.failure: A holdout is softened after a red run, so the product passes a weaker promise than the owner made.
signature_failures.guard: Treat any change to an expectation after a run as a promise change that needs a dated owner decision.

categories.name: Situated cognitions
categories.seam: Owns the participants a holdout is set inside; category 01 owns what was promised to them.

items.item_name: Cognition derived from planning evidence with provenance
items.detailed_description: Covers the situated cognition: a described participant in a described situation, derived from the project's planning evidence and the canon. Each cognition carries provenance to the documents it came from and is approved before holdouts are generated inside it. It matters because a holdout set inside an invented participant tests the agent's imagination, not the product's audience. Seam: item 0202 governs which kinds of participant the set must span.
synthesis_instructions: Derive each cognition from cited planning evidence and record the document and passage it came from.
Refuse to generate holdouts inside a cognition that has not been approved.
Never let a design lens add a participant trait that no planning evidence supports; record such a trait as a lens suggestion, not a fact.

internal_evaluation_criteria.question: Does every trait of the cognition trace to cited planning evidence or the canon?
internal_evaluation_criteria.pass_condition: Each trait resolves to a cited passage; an unsupported trait is marked as a lens suggestion or the cognition fails.
internal_evaluation_criteria.checklist: [ ] trace two traits of one cognition to their cited passages

applicability_signals: The task asks who will meet the product and in what situation
Planning documents describe users, operators, agents or integrations
anti_signals: No planning evidence exists yet; ask for it instead of inventing a participant

signature_failures.failure: A cognition is written from general knowledge, so its holdouts test a participant the product will never meet.
signature_failures.guard: Require a cited passage for every trait and approval before generation.

items.item_name: Participant span: human, agent, seam and the unknown future participant
items.detailed_description: Covers the breadth of the cognition set. The set spans the human who uses the product, the agent that calls it, the seam where two systems meet, and an unknown future participant whose needs are not yet written down. It matters because a set of only human users misses the agent and seam failures that agent-built products most often have. Seam: item 0201 governs the depth of one cognition; this item governs the span of the set.
synthesis_instructions: Check that the approved cognitions cover a human, an agent, a seam and an unknown future participant, and record each missing kind.
Refuse to call a cognition set complete while a participant kind is missing without an owner decision that excludes it.

internal_evaluation_criteria.question: Does the cognition set cover all four participant kinds, or record an owner exclusion for each missing one?
internal_evaluation_criteria.pass_condition: Each of human, agent, seam and future participant has a cognition or an owner exclusion; a silent gap fails.
internal_evaluation_criteria.checklist: [ ] tick each participant kind against the approved set

applicability_signals: A cognition set is proposed for approval
The product exposes an API, a protocol or a tool interface
anti_signals: The task concerns a single cognition's wording only

signature_failures.failure: Only human users are modelled, so failures at agent calls and system seams never meet a holdout.
signature_failures.guard: Check the four participant kinds before approval and record every exclusion as an owner decision.

categories.name: Sealed holdouts
categories.seam: Owns what is sealed and when; category 04 owns the randomness revealed at test time.

items.item_name: Publish the why, seal the how
items.detailed_description: Covers the split between the public and sealed halves of a holdout. The why (the promise and the cognition it protects) is published so the builder knows what matters. The how (the concrete inputs, steps and expected outputs) is sealed so the builder cannot tune to it. It matters because a builder who sees the how passes the test without serving the why. Seam: item 0302 governs when the seal is made; category 04 governs the parameters no one can know in advance.
synthesis_instructions: Publish each holdout's promise and cognition, and keep its concrete inputs, steps and expected outputs only in the sealed layer.
Refuse any brief, diagnostic or log that would show the builder a sealed input or expected output.
Report a failing holdout to the builder by its published why and a fixed diagnostic code, never by its sealed how.

internal_evaluation_criteria.question: Can anything the builder can read reveal a sealed input or expected output?
internal_evaluation_criteria.pass_condition: Briefs, diagnostics and logs carry only the published why and fixed codes; any sealed detail in them fails.
internal_evaluation_criteria.checklist: [ ] read one builder-facing diagnostic and confirm no sealed detail in it

applicability_signals: A holdout is being written, sealed or reported
A builder asks why a holdout failed
anti_signals: The holdout has been retired and its how is published on purpose

signature_failures.failure: A helpful failure message quotes the expected output, so the next build is tuned to it.
signature_failures.guard: Report failures only by published why and fixed diagnostic codes.

items.detailed_description: Covers the timing and form of the seal. The sealed plan is content-addressed and its commitment is recorded before the implementation it grades exists, so a later reader can confirm the holdout was not written to match the build. It matters because a holdout written after the build is a mirror. Seam: item 0301 governs what is sealed; this item governs proof of when.
synthesis_instructions: Record the sealed plan's content hash and the commit it was sealed at before implementation starts.
Refuse to accept a holdout whose seal cannot be shown to predate the implementation commit; mark it as not sealed.

internal_evaluation_criteria.question: Does the seal's recorded commitment predate the implementation it grades?
internal_evaluation_criteria.pass_condition: The commitment's commit is an ancestor of the implementation commit; a later or missing commitment fails.
internal_evaluation_criteria.checklist: [ ] compare the seal commit with the first implementation commit

applicability_signals: A holdout is about to grade an implementation
A sealed plan is created or changed
anti_signals: The task is an exploratory check that makes no acceptance claim

signature_failures.failure: A holdout is sealed after the build and certifies only that the build matches itself.
signature_failures.guard: Require a commitment that predates the implementation commit, checked from the history.

categories.name: Test-time randomness
categories.seam: Owns the private parameters drawn at test time; category 03 owns the sealed plan they complete.

items.item_name: Parameters bound to the evaluated commit and revealed only by the server
items.detailed_description: Covers the private random element of a test. Its parameters are drawn by a verifiable random function over the evaluated commit with a key the server holds, and they become known only when the test runs, through the server's reveal. It matters because a builder who can read the sealed plan could still pass a fixed test; parameters bound to the commit and to a server key cannot be learned in advance. Seam: item 0402 governs checking the parameters afterwards.
synthesis_instructions: Draw test-time parameters only through the server's reveal, bound to the commit being evaluated.
Refuse any parameter source the builder's role can read or compute before the test runs.
Never cache or log revealed parameters where the builder's role can read them.

internal_evaluation_criteria.question: Could the builder's role learn the parameters before the test runs?
internal_evaluation_criteria.pass_condition: The parameters depend on a server-held key and the evaluated commit, and the builder's role is refused the reveal; any other source fails.
internal_evaluation_criteria.checklist: [ ] confirm the builder role's reveal call is refused

applicability_signals: A test needs a value that must not be known in advance
A reveal call or parameter draw is designed or reviewed
anti_signals: The value is a fixed public fixture by design

signature_failures.failure: Parameters come from a seed in the repository, so the builder computes them and the test is fixed after all.
signature_failures.guard: Bind parameters to a server-held key and the evaluated commit, and refuse the builder role the reveal.

items.detailed_description: Covers the audit of a draw. After the test, anyone with the public key, the commit and the proof can verify the parameters were the function's output and not chosen to steer the result. It matters because a secret that cannot be checked afterwards is just trust. Seam: item 0401 governs secrecy before the test; this item governs verifiability after it.
synthesis_instructions: Record the proof, the public key and the commit with every verdict that used revealed parameters.
Refuse a verdict whose parameter proof does not verify, and name the proof that failed.

internal_evaluation_criteria.question: Does the parameter proof verify for this commit and public key?
internal_evaluation_criteria.pass_condition: The proof verifies and yields the recorded parameters; a missing or failing proof voids the verdict.

applicability_signals: A verdict is recorded or audited
Someone questions whether a test was steered
anti_signals: The test used no revealed parameters

signature_failures.failure: Parameters are kept but their proof is not, so no one can show the draw was not chosen.
signature_failures.guard: Store proof, public key and commit beside the verdict and verify on audit.

categories.name: Boundary observation
categories.seam: Owns how the product is observed; category 06 owns what is concluded from it.

items.item_name: Observe the product only at its boundary
items.detailed_description: Covers how an evaluator meets the product. The evaluator drives the real product through the interfaces its participants use (its command line, API, protocol or files) and observes only what crosses that boundary. It matters because a check that reaches into internals tests the implementation's structure, which the builder controls, rather than its behaviour. Seam: category 06 governs the verdict drawn from the observations.
synthesis_instructions: Drive the product only through interfaces a participant uses, and record each observation with the interface it crossed.
Refuse checks that import, patch or read the product's internals.
Never replace the product with a stub, mock or canned response during a holdout run.

internal_evaluation_criteria.question: Does every observation come from the product's public boundary?
internal_evaluation_criteria.pass_condition: Each observation names a participant-facing interface; an internal probe or a stub fails the run.
internal_evaluation_criteria.checklist: [ ] check the run's observations for any internal probe or stub

applicability_signals: A holdout is being run against a product
A check design is reviewed for what it touches
anti_signals: The task is a unit test the builder owns, not a holdout

signature_failures.failure: The check inspects an internal variable, so a refactor that keeps behaviour fails it and a broken interface passes it.
signature_failures.guard: Allow only boundary observations and record the interface of each.

categories.name: Verdicts
categories.seam: Owns the verdict and its record; category 05 owns the observations it rests on.

items.detailed_description: Covers the verdict when evidence is incomplete. A check that could not run, timed out, or produced an observation the evaluator cannot classify ends as a limitation or a failure, never as a pass. It matters because a pass by default rewards products that hide their behaviour. Seam: item 0602 governs how a verdict is recorded and accepted.
synthesis_instructions: Record every check that did not run to completion as a typed limitation, not a pass.
Refuse to report a holdout as passed while any of its checks is a limitation or unclassified.

internal_evaluation_criteria.question: Is any pass resting on a check that did not complete or could not be classified?
internal_evaluation_criteria.pass_condition: Every passed check completed and was classified; a pass over a limitation fails.
internal_evaluation_criteria.checklist: [ ] scan the verdict for limitations counted as passes

applicability_signals: A run ends with skipped, timed-out or unclassified checks
A summary reports a holdout result
anti_signals: Every check completed and was classified

signature_failures.failure: A missing tool or a timeout is reported as green, so the product passes a check that never ran.
signature_failures.guard: Type every incomplete check as a limitation and keep the verdict from passing.

items.item_name: Signed, replayable verdict accepted on an own rerun
items.detailed_description: Covers the record and acceptance of a verdict. The verdict is signed, names the commit, the sealed plan's hash and the parameter proof, and can be replayed. Acceptance is the reviewer's own rerun, not the author's report of a green. It matters because a reported pass is a claim, and a claim without a replayable record cannot be audited. Seam: item 0601 governs what counts as a pass.
synthesis_instructions: Record each verdict with the commit, the sealed plan's hash, the parameter proof and a signature.
Accept a verdict only after an independent rerun reproduces it; record the rerun beside it.
Refuse an acceptance that rests on the author's log alone.

internal_evaluation_criteria.question: Was the verdict accepted on an independent rerun that reproduced it?
internal_evaluation_criteria.pass_condition: An independent rerun with its own record reproduces the verdict; acceptance on the author's report fails.
internal_evaluation_criteria.checklist: [ ] find the independent rerun record and compare its result

applicability_signals: A verdict is about to be accepted or merged
An author reports that a holdout passed
anti_signals: The run is a local rehearsal that makes no acceptance claim

signature_failures.failure: An author's green is accepted without a rerun, so an environment-specific or fabricated pass is trusted.
signature_failures.guard: Require an independent rerun and a signed, replayable record before acceptance.

categories.name: Control measurement
categories.seam: Owns measured catch and false-pass rates; category 08 owns the authority they confer.

items.item_name: Catch rate and false-pass rate measured on known controls
items.detailed_description: Covers how a lens, cognition or check proves it works. It is run against known controls: products with a planted defect it should catch and products without one it should pass. Its catch rate and false-pass rate are recorded with their sample sizes. It matters because a check never shown to catch a known defect may catch nothing. Seam: category 08 governs what those rates allow the check to do.
synthesis_instructions: Measure each check against controls with and without a planted defect, and record catches, misses and sample sizes.
Refuse to report a catch rate without its sample size and the controls it came from.

internal_evaluation_criteria.question: Does the check have recorded catch and false-pass counts on named controls?
internal_evaluation_criteria.pass_condition: Counts and sample sizes exist for named controls; a rate without them fails.
internal_evaluation_criteria.checklist: [ ] read the check's control record and its sample size

applicability_signals: A new lens, cognition or check is introduced
Someone claims a check is effective
anti_signals: The check is still a draft that holds no authority

signature_failures.failure: A check is trusted because it sounds rigorous, though it has never caught a planted defect.
signature_failures.guard: Measure on known controls and record counts before the check holds any authority.

categories.name: Authority from bounds
categories.seam: Owns the authority a check holds; category 07 owns the measurements behind it.

items.item_name: Authority from the pessimistic bound, never assumed
items.detailed_description: Covers what a check may do with its result: advise, recommend or block. Its authority is computed from the pessimistic bound of its measured rates, so a check with few controls cannot block however good its point estimate looks. It matters because authority that is assumed, not earned, lets an untested check stop work or a broken one wave it through. Seam: category 07 governs the measurement; this item governs the decision rule.
synthesis_instructions: Compute each check's authority from the pessimistic bound of its measured catch and false-pass rates.
Refuse to let a check block on a point estimate alone; record the bound and the rule that set the authority.

internal_evaluation_criteria.question: Is the check's authority level derived from the pessimistic bound of its measured rates?
internal_evaluation_criteria.pass_condition: The recorded authority follows from the bound and the stated rule; an assumed or point-estimate authority fails.
internal_evaluation_criteria.checklist: [ ] recompute one check's authority from its recorded bound

applicability_signals: A check's result is about to block or approve work
Authority levels are set or changed
anti_signals: The check only advises and claims no authority

signature_failures.failure: A check measured on three controls blocks releases, so noise stops work.
signature_failures.guard: Derive authority from the pessimistic bound, which stays low until the sample is large enough.

categories.name: Planted falsifiers
categories.seam: Owns falsifiers the system plants to prove a check can fail; category 10 owns attacks by the builder.

items.item_name: A planted falsifier must be caught
items.detailed_description: Covers proving that a check can fail. Before a check is trusted, a falsifier (a deliberate defect, a fake citation, a thinned item) is planted where the check should see it, and the check must refuse it. It matters because a check that has never failed may be unable to. Seam: category 10 governs defects a builder introduces to win; this item governs defects the system plants to test itself.
synthesis_instructions: Plant at least one falsifier for each new check and record whether the check refused it.
Refuse to trust a check that passed its planted falsifier; replace or repair the check, not the falsifier.

internal_evaluation_criteria.question: Did the check refuse its planted falsifier?
internal_evaluation_criteria.pass_condition: A recorded run shows the check refusing the planted falsifier; a check that passed it fails.
internal_evaluation_criteria.checklist: [ ] find the falsifier run and its refusal

applicability_signals: A new check or judge is introduced
A check has never been seen to fail
anti_signals: The check's falsifier run is already recorded and unchanged since

signature_failures.failure: A judge passes everything, and nobody notices because no falsifier was planted.
signature_failures.guard: Plant a falsifier for every check and require the refusal on record.

categories.name: Gaming and leakage
categories.seam: Owns builder attempts to learn or steer a holdout; category 09 owns falsifiers the system plants itself.

items.item_name: The builder cannot learn the parameters or the sealed how before the test
items.detailed_description: Covers attacks on secrecy. An attacker in the builder's role tries every channel to learn the sealed how or the test-time parameters early: reading files, calling the reveal, inspecting logs, timing, or shared state with the sealed side on the same machine. It matters because one open channel defeats every seal. Seam: category 04 governs how parameters are drawn; this item governs attempts to learn them.
synthesis_instructions: Attempt each channel open to the builder's role (files, reveal calls, logs, shared state) and record whether it yields sealed content or parameters.
Report any channel that yields sealed content as a seal break, with the steps to reproduce it.

internal_evaluation_criteria.question: Did any channel open to the builder's role yield sealed content or parameters?
internal_evaluation_criteria.pass_condition: Every attempted channel is refused or yields nothing sealed; any leak fails the seal.
internal_evaluation_criteria.checklist: [ ] list the channels tried and the result of each

applicability_signals: A seal, a reveal path or a key store is designed or changed
The builder and the sealed side share a machine or user
anti_signals: The task asks you to weaken a seal rather than test it

signature_failures.failure: The seal is tested only through its front door, so a readable cache or log leaks the parameters.
signature_failures.guard: Try every channel open to the builder's role, not just the reveal call.

items.detailed_description: Covers grading against the system under test. A holdout whose expected outcome came from the product's own output, or from the validator's own oracle, proves only self-consistency. The adversary looks for such holdouts and for expected outcomes the builder could have produced. It matters because a self-oracled holdout passes a wrong but consistent product. Seam: item 1001 governs learning sealed content; this item governs where expected outcomes came from.
synthesis_instructions: Trace each expected outcome to its source and flag any that came from the product's own output or the validator's oracle.
Refuse a holdout whose ground truth is the system under test, and name the expectation that is self-oracled.

internal_evaluation_criteria.question: Does every expected outcome come from a source independent of the system under test?
internal_evaluation_criteria.pass_condition: Each expectation traces to an independent source; one taken from the product's output fails.
internal_evaluation_criteria.checklist: [ ] trace one expected outcome to its independent source

applicability_signals: Expected outcomes were generated by running the product
A golden file was refreshed from current output
anti_signals: The expectation is defined by an external specification quoted in the plan

signature_failures.failure: Golden files are regenerated from the build, so the holdout certifies whatever the build now does.
signature_failures.guard: Trace every expectation to an independent source and refuse regenerated goldens.

cross_cutting_postures.name: Provenance on every link
cross_cutting_postures.posture: Every holdout, cognition, parameter and verdict carries provenance back to an owner promise and its planning evidence; a link without provenance is a finding.

cross_cutting_postures.name: Deterministic where it can be
cross_cutting_postures.posture: Seals, digests and parameter proofs are deterministic and reproduce byte for byte on macOS and Linux; judgement is labelled as judgement and never reported as a deterministic result.

cross_cutting_postures.name: Secret hygiene
cross_cutting_postures.posture: Never print, log or paste a secret, a sealed layer or an unrevealed parameter; check only its presence and length.

cross_cutting_postures.name: Fail closed
cross_cutting_postures.posture: A check that could not run is a typed limitation, never a pass, and a limitation is reported with its cause.

module_laws.law: Never fabricate: no invented source, citation, hash, measurement or result.
Use claim-bound language: state exactly what was checked and no more.
Label each claim Verified, Probable or Open.
Record absence as absence; never invent around a missing input.
Quote sources exactly; never present a paraphrase as the source.

role_focus.identity: You are the holden planner: you turn the owner's promises and the project's planning evidence into approved situated cognitions and holdout plans, and you set how much authority each check holds.
You are the holden sealer: you seal the how of every holdout before the build and guard the test-time parameters until the server reveals them.
You are the holden evaluator: you run sealed holdouts against the real product at its boundary, record signed verdicts, and measure each check on known controls.
You are the holden adversary: you attack the seals, the reveal and the evaluator from the builder's position, and you plant falsifiers to prove each check can fail.
